purpose: exp-028 failed because the fixer wrote its own test, so the gate certified self-consistency. Test whether an INDEPENDENT tester (separate session, issue statement and parent tree only, never the fixer's tree or patch) makes the admission gate raise the hidden-test pass rate of the same cheap agent.
agent: Claude Code CLI, Haiku 5.5, --effort low; fixer 30 turns per attempt (exp-027 prompt, no test-writing instruction), tester 20 turns

arms.treatment: final fixer attempt after up to 2 gate-rejection retries

oracle_validity: the tester's tests count only if they exit 1 (assertion failures) on the parent source; the tester may be resumed once to repair an invalid test; tasks with no valid test are admitted ungated and reported as NoValidTest, never as passes of the gate

gate.G3: the tester's tests pass on the fixer's patched tree
gate.G4: the existing suite (tester files ignored) passes on the patched tree; NotRun and non-blocking if the parent suite is not green within 180 s
gate.feedback: on rejection the fixer is resumed with the pytest output tail only; the tester's source is never shown
gate.determinism: no model call inside the gate itself; the tester is a separate proposer whose output is checked by execution; hidden tests are never visible to tester, gate or feedback

primary_outcome: paired difference in hidden-test pass rate, final minus attempt 1, paired bootstrap 95% interval (10000 resamples, seed 20451074)
secondary: oracle coverage: fraction of tasks with a valid tester test
success_criteria: Pass iff the paired difference is >= +4 points and the interval lower bound is > 0. Inconclusive if the lower bound <= 0 and the point estimate > 0. Fail if the point estimate <= 0. No change to prompts, gate or thresholds after the first agent run; a failed design closes this candidate identity.
known_limits: tester and fixer are the same model family and read the same statement, so shared misreadings can still pass the gate
the statements were written from the hidden tests, which may make the tester unusually well aligned with the scoring tests relative to real deployment
providers may have seen these public commits (dated 2025-07-01 or later)
